summary: We are testing whether adding bitmap-based gap-filling to the existing skyline greedy packer improves the judge score for polyomino rectangle packing. The experiment compares a new variant (v8, with gap-filling) against the established v7 baseline (no gap-filling) that has scored 79-86 in prior iterations.
key_points: Two arms: h-main (v8 with bitmap gap-filling) and h-control-negative (v7 baseline without gap-filling). Each arm runs the judge once (~45s), producing a score from 0-100.

The hypothesis predicts v8 will score equal to or marginally better (0-2 points) than v7, since gap-filling targets internal voids below the skyline that non-rectangular pieces create. The expected improvement is small relative to ~5-point inter-run variance.

Confirmation: v8 scores ≥ v7 (or within noise). Refutation: v8 scores >3 points below v7, suggesting the bitmap overhead (cache pollution, slower inner loop) outweighs the density benefit. The diagnostic suggests checking whether v8 explores fewer width candidates if it underperforms.

Risk is low: this is an incremental single-mechanism test on top of a well-characterized baseline (skyline greedy + dynamic lookahead + column compaction + 3 orderings). No parameter tuning is involved — gap-filling is binary on/off.

Design is clean: no ablation arm needed (mechanism is atomic), no dose-response (binary feature). The two arms are sufficient to measure the gap-filling effect within the noise floor of the scoring system.
